papers.title: Male chickadees with better spatial cognition sire more extra-pair young.
papers.abstract: Across animal taxa, females commonly mate with more than one male, even in monogamous mating systems. These extra-pair copulations and resulting young may increase the fitness of the female via a variety of mechanisms. The 'good genes' hypothesis suggests that socially monogamous females mate outside their pair bond to increase the fitness of their offspring via indirect genetic benefits, because extra-pair males do not provide parental care. We tested this hypothesis by quantifying extra-pair paternity in nonmigratory, food-caching mountain chickadees (Poecile gambeli). Chickadees rely on spatial cognition to recover scattered food caches, and variation in spatial cognition is associated with increased survival, longer lifespan, and is heritable. However, less is known about the role of sexual selection on spatial cognitive abilities. In the current study, we found that (1) males with better spatial cognitive abilities sired more extra-pair young and produced heavier offspring in their own nests compared to their poorer-performing counterparts, and (2) extra-pair males had significantly better spatial cognition than the social males they cuckolded. These results suggest that sexual selection shapes the evolution of spatial cognition in food-caching chickadees and are consistent with the good genes hypothesis, which posits that females gain indirect genetic benefits via extra-pair young.

papers.title: Sexuality and healthcare: experiences of women with physical disabilities in Mabvuku, Harare.
papers.abstract: This study explores how women with physical disabilities experience and express sexuality, form intimate relationships, and navigate stigma, exclusion, and structural barriers in Mabvuku, Harare, a low-income suburb marked by poverty and limited infrastructure. Using the social model of disability, it challenges stereotypes that portray women with disabilities as asexual, dependent, or socially invisible. A qualitative design was employed, using purposive and referral sampling to recruit fifteen women with physical disabilities and five healthcare workers. Data were generated through a narrative analysis of life history interviews and key informant discussions, providing insights into the social, cultural, and institutional factors shaping participants' sexual lives. Findings revealed persistent sexual marginalisation driven by stigma, inaccessible infrastructure, exclusion from sexuality education, and experiences of violence and discrimination. Yet participants also demonstrated resilience and agency as they negotiated relationships and asserted aspects of sexual autonomy. The general disregard of their sexuality reflects systemic and societal barriers rather than individual limitations. Study findings call for disability-inclusive policies and attitudinal change in line with Zimbabwe's National Disability Policy and National Development Strategy 2, the African Disability Protocol, the Maputo Protocol, and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities.

papers.title: Keeping Score, Feeling Poor: Exchange Orientation Predicts Lower Relationship Satisfaction Through Diminished Gratitude.
papers.abstract: Past research shows that exchange orientation-the tendency to expect direct reciprocity in relationships-predicts lower romantic relationship well-being. However, less is known about why this transactional mindset, often grounded in seemingly reasonable ideals of fairness and balance, can be detrimental. This research examined gratitude and indebtedness as key emotional processes underlying the adverse effects of exchange orientation. Across five independent studies (N = 1,997), reduced felt gratitude consistently mediated the association between higher exchange orientation and lower romantic relationship satisfaction for both self and partner, emerging at both between- and within-person levels, cross-sectionally and longitudinally. In contrast, mediation via expressed gratitude was less consistent, and indebtedness generally failed to account for the link. These findings clarify why exchange orientation may undermine relationship well-being, identifying erosion of gratitude as a central pathway whereby individuals perceive relational benefits as running ledgers of obligations rather than spontaneous expressions of care and interdependence.

papers.title: Dye-based fluorescent organic nanoparticles: from chemistry to biology.
papers.abstract: Luminescent nanoparticles are readily becoming indispensable tools for bioimaging. Among the many luminescent nanoparticle variants available to date, dye-based fluorescent organic nanoparticles known as dFONs appear to be less known to the biological community than others. Yet, these single component objects, prepared by nano-aggregation of molecular dyes in water, offer several much sought-after properties. These include spontaneous water compatibility and high brightness, both necessary for state-of-the-art bioimaging. dFONs also display specificities such as extreme tunability, unique vectorisation capabilities and many other advantages to be discussed here. Since the last review of the dFONs litterature, dating back over a decade, significant advances have been made towards (i) tuning dFONs absorption and emission to the biological optical window, (ii) demanding bioimaging modalities such as single particle tracking and sensing and (iii) elegantly designed drug-delivery systems. Thanks to these recent developments, dFONs research should be blooming. Yet, it appears to be stuck at a proof-of-concept stage. We will discuss why this may be and propose avenues for taking up this exciting field's challenges. In doing so, we strive to help with dFONs dissemination to communities of both chemists interested in their design and biologists interested in their use.

papers.title: Forensic dating of thrombi in pulmonary embolism: neutrophil-to-macrophage ratio and bi-exponential modelling in an autopsy series.
papers.abstract: Thrombus dating is a relevant issue in forensic pathology, particularly in fatal pulmonary embolism (PE), where chronological assessment may contribute to the reconstruction of thromboembolic events and their medico-legal interpretation. This study aimed to investigate thrombus chronology in fatal PE by applying a quantitative neutrophil-to-macrophage (N/M) ratio model integrated with histological and immunohistochemical analysis. Twenty-six autopsy cases in which PE was certified as the cause of death were examined. Overall, 81 thrombi were analysed, including 67 pulmonary thrombi and 14 extrapulmonary venous thrombi. To assess temporal variability within thrombi, multiple anatomically distinct portions were sampled, resulting in the analysis of 162 histological samples. Thrombus age was estimated using a bi-exponential Levenberg-Marquardt N/M ratio model interpreted together with ancillary histological and immunohistochemical markers of thrombus organization. Estimated thrombus age ranged from less than 1 h to more than 10 days. Histological evidence of organization was predominantly observed in samples estimated to be older than 5 days. Several pulmonary thrombi exhibited complex internal stratification, with mural, central, and distal portions displaying substantially different estimated ages. Comparison between pulmonary and extrapulmonary venous thrombi revealed substantial temporal overlap, with no consistent chronological sequence identifiable across cases. In this autopsy series, thrombi of different estimated ages frequently coexisted, consistent with a multistage thromboembolic process. Application of the quantitative N/M ratio model provided a reproducible framework for early thrombus dating. These findings support the value of integrated thrombus analysis for forensic reconstruction and medico-legal evaluation of fatal PE.

papers.title: Label-Free Peptide Nucleic Acid-Based Electrocatalytic Biosensor Coupled with EXPAR for Ultrasensitive Detection of miR-181b.
papers.abstract: Osteosarcoma (OS) is the most common primary malignant bone tumor in adolescents. Diagnosis usually comes late because micrometastases are hard to see on imaging or in biopsy specimens. Exosomal microRNAs survive well in body fluids and have therefore become popular markers for liquid biopsy. miR-181b is abnormally expressed in OS, yet it occurs at low levels in body fluids and differs from miR-181a, miR-181c, and miR-181d by only a few bases. Measuring it demands both high sensitivity and high specificity. Here, we describe a label-free electrocatalytic electrochemical biosensor that pairs a peptide nucleic acid (PNA) capture probe with the exponential amplification reaction (EXPAR). A 3'-thiolated PNA probe was attached to a gold electrode by rapid freezing-assisted Au-S bonding. EXPAR converted the target into single-stranded DNA, which bound PNA and a signal probe to form a sandwich. PNA carries a neutral backbone, whereas DNA is negatively charged, so [Ru(NH3)6]3+ was adsorbed onto the sandwich by electrostatic attraction. [Fe(CN)6]3- then re-oxidized the reduced Ru complex in a catalytic cycle, and square wave voltammetry recorded the current. Under optimized conditions, the sensor responded linearly to miR-181b from 1 fM to 1 nM, with an experimental detection limit of 1 fM. It separated miR-181b from miR-181a, miR-181c, and miR-181d, and the inter-day RSD over 3 consecutive days was 4.34% (n = 9; three electrodes per day). After 6 days of storage in PBS at 4 °C, the electrodes still delivered 83.8% of their initial response. All measurements used synthetic miR-181b. Clinical validation and long-term shelf-life stability have not yet been established.

papers.title: Scaffold-guided generative AI for Type I photosensitizer design in hypoxic photodynamic therapy.
papers.abstract: Type I photosensitizers (PSs) are attractive for photodynamic therapy (PDT) of hypoxic tumors, but their development is limited by empirical modification and library screening. Here, we develop a scaffold-guided generative AI framework that couples Type I-specific prediction with controllable molecular generation for prospective PS design. AI-assisted literature mining and molecular structure recognition were first used to construct a curated data set of 1338 PSs. Subsequently, we developed BiCAM-PS, a cross-attention model integrating molecular graphs, fingerprints, and physicochemical descriptors, which achieved an accuracy of 93.3% and an ROC-AUC of 0.9633 for Type I classification under the random split. We further established PSGenerator, a scaffold decorator that generates structurally diverse molecules around predefined attachment sites, enabling prediction-guided exploration of Type I PS chemical space. Using a redesigned tetracyclic scaffold as a test case, the framework prioritized six synthetically accessible candidates, all of which experimentally exhibited Type I characteristics. Among them, A1 showed efficient radical ROS generation, strong photostability, mitochondrial localization, and potent photodynamic activity under both normoxic and hypoxic conditions, markedly suppressing 4T1 tumor growth in vivo without obvious systemic toxicity. Together, this work establishes a data-driven framework that advances Type I PS discovery from empirical molecular modification and library screening toward prospective generative design.

papers.title: Dimeric architectures of Chlamydia pneumoniae and Moraxella catarrhalis glutamyl tRNA synthetases.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.abstract: The glutamyl-tRNA synthetases (GluRSs) in Moraxella are predicted to be members of a subfamily of dimeric GluRSs. However, an amino acid substitution at an interhelical asparagine bridge near a hinge axis relating the extended and bent folds of monomeric and dimeric GluRSs, respectively, led us to hypothesize that these synthetases dimerize using a distinct fold. The GluRSs in Chlamydia are nondiscriminatory and are also predicted to form dimers while displaying unique amino acid usage in their anticodon-binding domains. Here, we utilized a combination of x-ray crystallography, size-exclusion chromatography, multi-angle light scattering, and small-angle x-ray scattering to characterize the GluRSs from Moraxella catarrhalis and Chlamydia pneumoniae. Four crystal structures are reported in detail, including that of apo McGluRS, and CpGluRS in both apo and ligand-bound states. Both enzymes form homodimers and show an ordered C-terminal extension. The extensions contain an α-helix of similar length and place a lysine or glutamine residue at the end of the helix beyond a conserved lysine-rich consensus motif. The McGluRS fold displays a decompressed interhelical kink close to its hinge axis. The anticodon-binding domain and catalytic domain, including the ATP loop, couple through different amino acid residues in the two enzymes. The anticodon-binding site of CpGluRS displays unique secondary structure and hydrogen bonding. Conformational changes that occur upon binding a structural analog of glutamyl adenylate extend to a region near the tRNA A76-binding site that contains a glutamine residue conserved in dimeric GluRSs.

papers.title: Aggregating nanoplastics transport with nonlinear attachment: Model evaluation against published experimental data.
papers.abstract: The established transport model of Katzourakis and Chrysikopoulos is extended to aggregating nanoplastics in water-saturated porous media under one dimensional flow. Nanoplastics may remain suspended or attach to the solid matrix through reversible and/or irreversible retention. To capture particle size evolution, the Smoluchowski population balance equation is coupled with the advection dispersion attachment equations, accounting for the effect of aggregate size on attachment and retention. The model was evaluated using published batch and column data for nanoplastics (10-30 mg/L) in seawater-saturated sea sand, including surface functionalized particles with humic acid and pristine particles with algae polysaccharides. Unlike conventional approaches that assume constant size colloids, the transport model is constrained by aggregation parameters derived independently from batch experiments and held fixed during fitting. The model also accounts for aggregation in the source container during injection, so the inlet particle size distribution may evolve with time. These extensions link the batch and transport experiments in one consistent framework. Aggregation can strongly influence breakthrough behavior, and information criteria comparisons with non-aggregating models showed that fixed size models may fail to reproduce complex breakthrough profiles. The model provides a more physically realistic basis for analyzing nanoplastic fate and transport in porous media.

papers.title: Greater Perceived Partner Support Is Associated With Higher Fecundability.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Social support is a key determinant of health, and romantic partners are an important source of such support; yet few studies have examined the effect of partner support on fertility. OBJECTIVE: To examine the association between the degree of perceived partner support and fecundability, and whether it varies by infertility history, pregnancy attempt time at enrollment and diagnosed depression. METHODS: We used data from Pregnancy Study Online (PRESTO), an internet-based North American prospective preconception cohort (2013-2025). Participants were aged 21-45 years, assigned female at birth and attempting conception with one partner without fertility treatment (n = 9182). We measured two types of perceived past-year partner support using questions adapted from the Berkman-Syme Social Network Index: degree of partner love and affection, and degree of partner emotional support. We followed participants for up to 12 months or until pregnancy, using proportional probabilities regression to estimate fecundability ratios (FRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs), adjusting for confounders. We stratified by infertility history, attempt time at enrollment, and diagnosed depression and examined the mediating role of intercourse frequency. RESULTS: Fecundability was higher among those reporting receiving love and affection from their partners some of the time (FR 1.16, 95% CI 0.89, 1.52), most of the time (FR 1.38, 95% CI 1.08, 1.76) or all the time (FR 1.49, 95% CI 1.17, 1.90), relative to never or rarely. Associations for emotional support followed a similar monotonic pattern but were weaker (all the time: FR 1.36, 95% CI 1.17, 1.57). Both associations were stronger among participants with an infertility history, longer attempt times at enrollment and diagnosed depression. papers.title: Sexual wellbeing in Britain: findings from the fourth National Survey of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles (Natsal-4).
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Sexual wellbeing is an individual state of feeling respected, safe, and comfortable with sex and sexuality, and having self-esteem, agency, and support in one's sexual life. It is related to, but distinct from, sexual function and sexual health. The epidemiology of sexual wellbeing in a general population is not well understood. We aimed to examine inequalities in low sexual wellbeing, and discover associations with sexual behaviour, sexual and reproductive health experiences, and general and mental health. We sought to understand which individual items within our validated 13-item measure of sexual wellbeing (the Natsal-SW) are most strongly associated with key sexual health behaviours and indicators. METHODS: We conducted the fourth National Survey of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles (Natsal-4), which is a large nationally representative cross-sectional study of people aged 16-59 years who are resident in Britain (data used here collected between Sept 20, 2022, and Dec 3, 2023). 4160 participants reporting sexual experience ever completed the Natsal-SW; standardised score range 0-52, low selected as ≤33, and high as ≥48. Focusing attention on those with most need, we used age-adjusted logistic regressions to examine associations with low sexual wellbeing. FINDINGS: The weighted prevalence of current low sexual wellbeing was similar in women (14·3% [95% CI 12·6-16·3]) and men (13·7% [11·7-15·9]), but high sexual wellbeing was slightly less prevalent in women than men (20·7% [95% CI 18·7- 22·8] vs 24·4% [21·8- 27·1]; p=0·024). Nine items on Natsal-SW differed by gender; notably women were more likely to report feeling upset with others about past sexual events, and men to report feeling ashamed about sexual thoughts. papers.title: Beyond Food Insecurity: Coercive Scarcity Among Black Women Experiencing Intimate Partner Violence.
papers.abstract: Black women experiencing intimate partner violence (IPV) may face intersecting racialized and material constraints that shape not only whether food is available but also the conditions under which it can be obtained. This cross-sectional study examined associations between everyday discrimination and three distinct food-related outcomes among 187 Black women with histories of IPV: food insecurity, staying with an abusive partner to access food, and engaging in sex to access food or money for food. Everyday discrimination was assessed with the nine-item Everyday Discrimination Scale. In adjusted analyses, greater everyday discrimination was associated with higher odds of food insecurity (aOR = 1.06, 95% CI [1.03, 1.10]), staying with an abusive partner to access food (aOR = 1.04, 95% CI [1.01, 1.07]), and engaging in sex to access food or money for food (aOR = 1.05, 95% CI [1.02, 1.09]). We interpret this pattern through coercive scarcity, an emerging conceptual lens for considering how intersecting structural disadvantage and interpersonal violence may narrow safe and viable options for meeting basic needs. Coercive scarcity was not directly measured in this study. Findings suggest that prevention and intervention efforts should move beyond identifying food insecurity alone to attend to the conditions under which essential resources are secured. Integrating food and economic supports with IPV services, reducing barriers to assistance, and strengthening coordination across violence, housing, healthcare, and food-support systems may help expand safe and viable pathways for meeting basic needs.

papers.title: Caring for Women Experiencing Intimate Partner Violence During the Breastfeeding Period: A Reflective Lifeworld Study.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Intimate partner violence (IPV) is a major global challenge and a threat to health and wellbeing. Previous research suggests that caring has the potential to be an existential refuge for women experiencing IPV during the breastfeeding period. In Sweden, breastfeeding care and support are provided both by healthcare professionals and by breastfeeding peer supporters. However, little is known about their lived experience of caring in this context. AIM: The study aims to describe the meaning of caring for women experiencing IPV during the breastfeeding period, from the perspectives of healthcare professionals and breastfeeding peer supporters. APPROACH AND METHODS: The study adopts a Reflective Lifeworld Research approach. Lifeworld interviews with fourteen midwives, district nurses, and/or breastfeeding peer supporters were analysed phenomenologically. The Swedish Ethical Review Authority approved the study, and all participants gave their informed consent. RESULTS: The essential meaning of caring for women experiencing IPV during breastfeeding is navigating a constrained caring space, further described through its constituents: negotiating partners' invading presence; counterbalancing IPV exposedness; experiencing conflicting caring roles, necessitating a new caring approach; sharing a solitary responsibility; handling possibilities and limitations of caring space; and strengthening one's caring intuition through experience. CONCLUSIONS: Caring, in the context of IPV during breastfeeding, means navigating a constrained caring space, invaded by the partners. Healthcare professionals and breastfeeding peer supporters strive to maintain a focus on women, children, and breastfeeding, yet are often required to adapt to partners' needs, resulting in breastfeeding care being given lower priority. Responding to child abuse and neglect in Norwegian schools: Responsibility and scope for action in light of children's lived experiences.
papers.abstract: This qualitative study explores how teachers and school nurses in Norwegian compulsory education (Grades 3-10) perceive their mandate and scope for action when responding to child abuse and neglect (CAN), including childhood exposure to intimate partner violence (CEIPV). Drawing on 17 individual interviews and three focus groups with 25 teachers and school nurses, analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis, the study identified three themes: responsibility beyond expectations, caring under constraints, and unrecognized potential for care. The professionals' accounts were interpreted through a children's rights framework and contextualized through children's lived experiences reported in an earlier study from the same research project. The findings highlight professionals' strong sense of responsibility for supporting and protecting children exposed to CAN, the institutional and organizational constraints on their scope for action, and the potential for support at school. Contextualized through children's lived experiences, the findings draw attention to predictability, stable relationships, tailored support, participation, and academic engagement as important dimensions of children's everyday school life. Taken together, these perspectives suggest that the school's potential for support and protection lies not only in formal responses, but also in sustaining the relational, pedagogical, and social support available at school. Recognizing and supporting these relational, pedagogical, and social dimensions of school practice, alongside clear roles, relevant knowledge, collaboration, and organizational support, may strengthen the school's protective role for children exposed to CAN.
